aggregationTypes.heading: Basic information on the complex export
aggregationTypes.paragraph1: The complex export of species traits allows exporting original, inherited, aggregated or merged values. Original values are those that individual taxa had stated for the given trait in the default data file. However, these original values are not stated for all taxa. There are cases where values are given e.g. for a subspecies but not for the parent species. In such cases, inherited or aggregated values can be used. The process of inheritance runs down the taxonomic tree and values are transferred only to so-called singletons, i.e. taxa that are the only ones within the parent taxon. For such a taxon, the inherited values then contain all the data that can be found in the original values when looking up towards the root of the tree, as long as the parents are also singletons. The process of aggregation, on the other hand, runs up the taxonomic tree. There are several ways in which the values stated for taxa are aggregated. These aggregation methods are described precisely with the individual aggregation types. The export can include original, inherited and aggregated values at once and export them as so-called merged values. In that case, original values take precedence over aggregated ones and aggregated values take precedence over inherited ones. If no field of the offered values is checked during the export, original, inherited and aggregated values are exported automatically.
aggregationTypes.paragraph2: When exporting, it is also possible to choose a list of taxa for which to export the values. If no taxa are chosen, all are exported automatically. As the last option, the user can select the taxonomic ranks to include in the export. If none are checked, all are exported automatically.
aggregationTypes.paragraph3: The exact way of exporting the individual values (original, inherited, aggregated) is given by the aggregation type set for each trait. The list of the individual aggregation types is given below.
aggregationTypes.title: Aggregation types
